# Finance Process Analysis (Deloitte + DUVo) — Input for the Global AI-Initiative Registry

**Date**: 2026-10-19 (afternoon; inferred from "recordings due tomorrow" vs. the 20 Oct deadline and "today's afternoon")
**Attendees**: Tomáš Kořenek (Dr. Max CZE, accounting at Česká lékárna holding), Hana Stanislavová (ViaPharma CZE, accounting), Jindřich Tůma (BigHub / Dr. Max AI ambassador, host), Marek Pillár (BigHub, PM; joined a few minutes late because of a Teams issue)
**Type**: external
**Recording**: N/A (Teams transcript, pasted)
**Previous session**: N/A (first meeting). Related: [2026-10-16 Švarcová (Brno accounting)](2026-10-16-svarcova-brno-accounting-lexie-2027-initiatives.md), where Deloitte's accounting review first came up.

For example, the line where Jindřich introduces himself as AI ambassador is labelled "Kořenek", and "pane Kořenku" is said under the "Kořenek" label. ## TL;DR

Jindřich needed input for Dr. Max's new **global AI-initiative registry**, which Dudaško presents as CIO at the global meeting on Wed 2026-10-21. Two of the CZ initiatives were unknown to him, and both are linked to DUVo. This meeting covered one of them: the **finance process analysis** that **Deloitte** runs on the **DUVo** platform for Dr. Max (Česká lékárna holding) and ViaPharma. It is an analysis, not a delivery project. Outputs are a process map, a list of processes suited to automation or AI, and **2 agentic pilots** (one per company, around mid-to-late November). **Benefits are not defined yet.** Deloitte's early 0.2–0.4 FTE estimate is considered inflated and is internal only. Finance gave candid, mostly negative feedback on DUVo and Deloitte's method, and is conservative about AI in accounting. The owner, **Pavel Hofman**, is away until the end of October.

## Key Discussion Points

### 1. Why the meeting: the global AI-initiative registry

- **Jindřich**: Dr. Max is building a **registry of all AI initiatives across all countries**. Each one lists its benefits, quantified in money, time or FTE, or framed as a capability such as a predictive model. Dudaško presents it as CIO. Jindřich (AI ambassador: coordinating AI projects and adoption, plus the AI Platform, about half BigHub and half Dr. Max) can fill in all BigHub initiatives. Two remained that he knew nothing about, both linked to DUVo: the **finance redesign** and one other, which was not covered here. Dudaško asked him to get the row filled. Jindřich got the contact for Pavel Hofman from Dudaško, but Hofman is on holiday, so the meeting went ahead with his team.

### 2. What the finance project is

- **Kořenek**: the goal is to map the processes in Dr. Max's accounting team (pharmacy accountants and overhead accountants) and propose where AI or agents could make work more efficient. He doesn't know the specific targets (FTE or money); Hofman would. He sees it as a **"reconnaissance by battle"** `[translated from Czech]`: a trial of whether this tool and approach work and could then be repeated in Slovakia and other countries, which is also how Deloitte and DUVo want to earn money. He thinks registering it as an initiative card is **premature**.
- **Scope**: both CZ companies, Dr. Max retail (Česká lékárna holding) and ViaPharma distribution.
- **Status**: Deloitte reports the pharmacy-accountant inputs are 100% recorded and the overhead accountants 98% (2 sub-processes left). Dr. Max's recordings are due **tomorrow (2026-10-20)**, ViaPharma's two days later. The project started at the **end of September** so it could capture the October month-end close.
- **Agreed summary (Jindřich, confirmed by Kořenek and Stanislavová)**:
  1. Analysed finance processes for Dr. Max and ViaPharma.
  2. A list of processes suitable for automation, AI or agents, with a suitability assessment.
  3. **2 agentic pilots** (one per company), included in the contract price as demonstrations. Horizon is around mid-to-late November (Kořenek: "mid or 20 November", not months).
- **Next steps for Deloitte**: first analyses next week, then numeric benefit and saving estimates in the following weeks. At least 2 more rounds of targeted follow-up questions on processes with potential. Which recommendations get implemented will depend on cost, risks and benefits.
- **ERP upgrade**: next year Dr. Max likely moves to a new version of its accounting ERP, which is heavily customised. Finance wants to use the analysis results in that upgrade even if they don't implement them now.

### 3. Benefits: none defined, early estimate considered inflated

- Deloitte's first estimate for one process was **0.2–0.4 of an accountant's FTE** (Kořenek also said "a tenth of an FTE"). On reflection, finance thinks it is **inflated**, because the hours saved don't add up. He reads it as Deloitte needing to show something attractive for its fee. Small gains could add up across about 20 pharmacy and 20 overhead processes, but "today it would be guessing" `[translated from Czech]`.
- **Jindřich told Marek not to use the number**: it is an analysis only, and benefits will come from Deloitte's final output. Marek confirmed it stays internal.
- **Kořenek**: expectations should be tempered. Accounting already has a high level of automation (RPA bots for about 5 years). A previous Deloitte analysis was done 1–2 years ago. Nobody expects it to "cut a third of the accountants". The team's only KPI is a correct month-end close on time.

### 4. Feedback on DUVo and Deloitte's method (candid)

- **Kořenek, Deloitte**: added little value. They fed Dr. Max's manuals and job descriptions to AI, which split them into dozens and eventually hundreds of processes, and loaded those into DUVo, including processes Dr. Max said were irrelevant or rare (a few minutes a few times a year). Revisions happened on the fly under time pressure. He sees this as the **intermediary (Deloitte) failing, not DUVo**.
- **Kořenek, DUVo itself**:
  - At first, an accountant with 20 processes got 20 e-mails with no clear status. This was later fixed to one e-mail with a checklist. It "felt like they were learning on us" `[translated from Czech]`.
  - Each process takes **20–30 min of real-time recording and commentary**. It doesn't run in the background, so people effectively do their work twice, during the month-end close.
  - DUVo's questions are often beside the point. It asks accountants about inventory shortfalls or KPIs, and misses what matters.
  - It takes a sample of **8 of ~20 accountants** who do identical work (about 23 pharmacies each). That is useful only for spotting shortcuts.
  - The recording picks up speech within 3–5 m, which disrupts the semi-open-space office. Nobody warned them, so they moved recordings to home office.
  - He had hoped recording could run during work, with commentary after the close (after about the 10th–12th of the month).
- **Stanislavová (ViaPharma)**:
  - The purpose wasn't explained upfront ("give us your processes"), so the process descriptions didn't fit the recording format.
  - Not all accountants can present their work, even with manuals.
  - DUVo's write-ups contain many "serious errors" she doesn't recognise. Colleagues who fixed 3 errors then got 4.
  - Stable, programmed processes were documented for nothing.
  - A consultant sitting with them would have understood the processes better.
  - Method: she reviewed and rewrote about 67 manuals. Each accountant uploads the manual to DUVo and presents it on real data, and DUVo asks follow-up questions. Less tech-savvy colleagues record in her office with a helper.
  - **Positives**: the internal review of all processes surfaced better ways of working. DUVo repeatedly flags **single-person dependency** (only one person does a process). The ViaPharma pilot Deloitte picked is good; she had pointed it out herself.
- **Jindřich**: similar view. He likes the vision, since process analysis is important and hard, but DUVo is "still in nappies" `[translated from Czech]` and needs a human touch (diagram edits etc.).

### 5. AI vs. automation in accounting

- **Kořenek** is conservative and "not a fan of AI" in accounting, where entries drive taxes and audits and need maximum accuracy. He prefers clear, rule-based automation and asked whether RPA counts as AI.
- **Jindřich**: in an ideal sequence, clean the data first, then analyse all processes, then automate and digitise with connected tools, and add AI last for the logic layer. Example: Reklamace automation plus AI drafting supplier e-mails. Agreed accounting is the most sensitive area for changes.
- **Marek**: any problem can be addressed with AI, but under the **AI Act** critical outputs (sensitive data, a signed financial close) always need a **human in the loop** who reviews and approves before anything is delivered.
- **Marek** also started to offer BigHub's human-led process analysis alongside DUVo. **Jindřich cut this short**: the meeting was only to understand the project for the registry.

### 6. Contacts

- **Deloitte** (practical side): **Drahoňovský** (finance). Partners overseeing: Kardoš and Kaválek (uncertain spelling).
- Delivery side (ViaPharma at least): **Barbora Neumannová**. Kořenek shared the contacts in the chat. It's unclear whether she is with Deloitte or DUVo.
- **Pavel Hofman** (finance; owns the initiative) is away until the end of October. Contact him in early November.

## Decisions Made

- The registry row for the finance initiative is framed as an **analysis**: Deloitte, via DUVo, analyses current finance processes at Dr. Max and ViaPharma, assesses suitability for automation and AI, and runs 2 demonstration pilots. **Benefits stay -tbd-** until Deloitte delivers. Jindřich fills it in for Wednesday's global meeting.
- Deloitte's early 0.2–0.4 FTE estimate is **not used** anywhere (internal, considered inflated).

## Sentiment & Tone

Polite and cooperative, but finance was openly critical. Kořenek was frank about Deloitte's method and DUVo's disruption during the month-end close, sceptical of the benefit numbers, and conservative about AI in accounting. He is pro-automation and anti-"creativity". Stanislavová was more balanced and credited the exercise for forcing an internal process review. Jindřich kept the tone light (an opening mix-up with a wrong invitee) and stayed on the registry goal, cutting off Marek's pitch, which was the right call for a first contact. Relational signal: finance sees outside consultants as knowing less than its own long-tenured team. Any future BigHub involvement should come in with humility, rule-based automation first, and human-in-the-loop by design. There is also a competitive read: DUVo's AI-only, recording-based method is struggling here. A human-led analysis (BigHub's approach) is a credible contrast, but only once it is invited.
